newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Thursday on overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 19,750 yuan ($2,382) per tonne, losing 50 yuan.
It opened at 19,700 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 19,900 yuan and a low of 19,680 yuan per tonne.
August fell 290 to 19,650, September 200 to 19,620, October 60 to 19,740, December 140 to 19,710 and the January 1998 contract 20 to 19,850 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 82,320 tonnes from 64,400 tonnes.
Copper opened lower and fell further for most of the session, traders said.
Traders said ongoing losses on the LME were dampening Shanghai market sentiment, which had been hit after copper fell below the key 20,000-yuan support level on Wednesday.
"Many investors believed copper would continue to fall due to current weak demand, resulting in more stop loss selling today," one trader said.
"The LME losses shattered investors' dreams of a short-term rebound," he added.
Benchmark three months LME copper ended Wednesday at $2,267 per tonne, off $11 from Tuesday's close but up sharply from a $2,247 early low.
Increases in LME copper stocks on Thursday of 13,025 tonnes saw the price slip to a five-month low in early trading of $2,226 with a backwardation of $140/150.
In Shanghai, physical copper prices fell to 19,700 yuan on Thursday from 19,900-20,000 yuan on Wednesday due to the poor performance of futures.
Traders said technical charts indicated copper futures would have a hard time rising above 20,000 yuan in the short term.
"Copper has run into in a downward channel and any rebound would be a good chance to build short positions," a second trader said.
August fell 140 to 13,280, September 300 to 13,200, October 260 to 13,200, November 340 to 13,200 and December 260 to 13,200 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 5,600 tonnes from 3,020 tonnes.
